rounds.text: Bank of Maharashtra is trading at a compelling valuation with a P/E of 9.38x against a sector benchmark of 18.09x [E1, E6]. This low valuation is coupled with exceptional profitability, highlighted by a return on equity of 22.6% and a 5-year median return on equity of 20%, significantly outperforming the sector benchmark ROE of 5.51% [E9, E11, E25]. The business demonstrates remarkable fundamental momentum, delivering compounded profit growth of 65% over 5 years and 31% over the trailing twelve months, which comfortably outpaces its 37% compounded share price growth over the same 5-year period [E17, E19, E21, E47]. Furthermore, institutional backing is expanding rapidly as foreign institutions increased their holding to 6.50% from 0.45% and domestic institutions rose to 13.76% from 4.71% since December 2023 [E33, E34]. Conceded: operating cash flow is negative at Rs -11,336 Cr for March 2026, leading to a negative cash conversion of -1.62x [E28, E29].

Despite reported profitability, Bank of Maharashtra exhibits severe cash generation anomalies, highlighted by an operating cash flow of Rs -11,336 Cr and a free cash flow of Rs -11,742 Cr for March 2026, leading to a deeply negative cash conversion ratio of -1.62x [E28, E29, E30]. Fundamental solvency and quality indicators flash explicit warnings, specifically pointing to a low interest coverage ratio, potentially capitalized interest costs, an abnormally low tax rate, and massive contingent liabilities totaling Rs 50,756 Cr [E52, E53, E54, E55]. Furthermore, the bank's return on capital employed sits at a modest 6.0%, failing to stand out against a sector median ROCE of 6.1% [E10, E68]. Insiders and major owners are steadily reducing their stake, with promoter holdings dropping from 86.46% in December 2023 down to 73.60% by September 2026 [E32]. Valuation risk is compounded by a price-to-book ratio of 2.11x, which outpaces the sector benchmark of 1.23x [E7], alongside earnings growth that is formally flagged as decelerating by the signal engine [E61]. Conceded: the company maintains a high return on equity of 22.6% alongside a 19.4% dividend payout ratio [E11, E51].

Conceded: operating cash flow and free cash flow for March 2026 are negative at Rs -11,336 Cr and Rs -11,742 Cr respectively, with a cash conversion of -1.62x [E28, E29, E30], alongside contingent liabilities of Rs 50,756 Cr [E54]. However, the bear's claim of a modest ROCE fails to acknowledge that the company achieves an outstanding ROE of 22.6% and a median 5-year ROE of 20%, vastly outperforming the sector benchmark ROE of 5.51% [E9, E11, E25]. While the bear points to promoter stake reduction, this has been actively absorbed by institutional buyers, with foreign institutions increasing their holdings to 6.50% and domestic institutions rising to 13.76% alongside positive institutional money flow [E32, E33, E34, E35]. The valuation concern regarding price-to-book is balanced by a compelling P/E ratio of 9.38x to 9.39x, sitting at a steep discount to the sector benchmark of 18.09x [E1, E6]. Furthermore, the bear ignores robust long-term and short-term fundamentals, including 5-year compounded profit growth of 65% and TTM profit growth of 31%, which confirm that strong underlying performance continues to outpace sector medians [E17, E19, E66].

Conceded: the company achieves a 5-year median ROE of 20% and an ROE of 22.6%, outperforming the sector benchmark ROE of 5.51% [E9, E11, E25]. However, citing these returns ignores that ROCE sits at a weak 6.0% [E10], matching the sector median ROCE of 6.1% [E68]. While institutional buyers increased stakes as promoters reduced holdings to 73.60% [E32, E33, E34], this ownership shift coincides with a severe drop in operating cash flow to Rs -11,336 Cr and free cash flow to Rs -11,742 Cr in March 2026 [E29, E30]. The bull highlights a P/E of 9.38x against the sector benchmark of 18.09x [E1, E6], but ignores that the price-to-book ratio of 2.11x trades at a sharp premium to the sector benchmark of 1.23x [E7]. Furthermore, recent price growth exceeding profit growth by 37% indicates that expectations are running ahead of delivery [E48], while the screening engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E61].

Conceded: ROCE sits at 6.0% [E10] and the price-to-book ratio is 2.11x against the sector benchmark of 1.23x [E7]. However, dismissing the extraordinary ROE of 22.6% [E11] by focusing on ROCE ignores that the company vastly outpaces the sector benchmark ROE of 5.51% [E9]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows were negative in March 2026 [E29, E30], yet institutional accumulation by both foreign and domestic entities has surged significantly from late 2023 levels [E33, E34], driving a positive institutional money flow signal [E35]. Furthermore, while the bear flags decelerating earnings growth [E61], the business maintains stellar multi-year profit compounding of 65% over 5 years and 39% over 3 years [E17, E18], supported by an 85 out of 100 rules-based screen score with medium buy confidence [E56].

Conceded: the company vastly outpaces the sector benchmark ROE of 5.51% with its reported ROE of 22.6% [E9, E11], and institutional money flow shows positive accumulation [E35]. However, the bull's reliance on ROE obscures severe underlying capital generation issues, notably a dismal ROCE of 6.0% and a low interest coverage ratio [E10, E52]. Furthermore, pointing to multi-year profit compounding [E17, E18] dismisses the explicit warning that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E61]. The bull downplays the catastrophic operational reality of March 2026, where operating cash flow collapsed to Rs -11,336 Cr and free cash flow dropped to Rs -11,742 Cr [E29, E30]. Finally, while foreign and domestic institutional holdings increased since late 2023 [E33, E34], promoter ownership simultaneously plummeted by 12.86 percentage points down to 73.60% [E32].
